_comment: Worked example — the PR-290 (ABC-45, a worked feature) storyboard. Schema + rules: steps/1-storyboard.md; diagram rules: diagrams.md. Beat 1 is ALWAYS the motivation, in the reporter's words from the ticket (quote + reportedSymptom + affected + impact + narration); capture-beats.mjs refuses the storyboard without it or with it anywhere else, and refuses a generic/empty line. The intro card comes from .title/.subtitle; a static beat can carry heading/bullets/footer for a real summary card instead of one run-on caption. The two source:image beats are Mermaid diagrams rendered by scripts/render-diagrams.mjs — architecture first, then the ERD, both after the motivation and before the first BEFORE beat. A diagram beat's holdMs is ignored: it lives max(6, voice + 1.8) s.
title: ABC-45 · PR #290
subtitle: Email for every Stripe event

beats.quote: Every time a client pays by bank transfer, the invoice stays open and finance has no idea the money arrived.
beats.reportedSymptom: the invoice stays open and finance has no idea
beats.narration: The finance team said it plainly: when a client pays by bank transfer, the invoice stays open, finance has no idea, and money sits unreconciled for days.

beats.caption: ARCHITECTURE — org's own Stripe account → webhook → notification
beats.narration: Here is the shape of it: the product bills through its own Stripe account, Stripe calls our webhook, and the webhook is the only place this fix lives.

beats.caption: DATA MODEL — invoice raises billing_notification rows
beats.narration: The change reads invoice, writes billing_notification, and keys the row on invoice_id. One event, one row — that is what makes a redelivery cheap to ignore.

beats.caption: INV-001035 · $5,000 · open — billed through the org's own Stripe account
beats.narration: the product lets a company bill its clients through its own Stripe account. This invoice is open and waiting to be paid. Stripe sends a webhook for every step of that payment.

beats.caption: BEFORE — payment_intent.processing landed: pending, and Billing is empty
beats.narration: Here is one of the gaps. The client pays by bank transfer, the handler moves the invoice to pending, and nothing else happens. No email, nothing in the app.

beats.caption: AFTER — Payment Pending from Initech, delivered to owner@acme.com
beats.narration: With the fix the same event fires a new billing notification, by email and in app, naming the client, the amount, the invoice and the organization.

box.text: A bank transfer for invoice INV-001035

beats.caption: AFTER — the same event in the app, linked to the invoice
beats.narration: In the app it is the same story: a billing notification linked straight to the invoice. The type is data driven, so it appears under Billing with no frontend change.

beats.caption: Redelivery guard — three more identical events, still one email
beats.narration: Webhooks get redelivered, so a new email risks a duplicate. Three more identical events, and the count is still one.
One new notification type. One additive migration. No existing email touched. That is pull request two ninety.
